regions.label: Figure B4.3.1 — Public intent and private intent data can be combined to detect illegal fishing activity
regions.summary: Infographic shows how satellite imagery and vessel AIS data can be combined to identify and track fishing vessels. Satellite sources detect vessels or lights and provide coverage; AIS provides vessel locations and movements.
regions.details: A circular, four-part infographic surrounds a central vessel. The upper-left section depicts daytime high-resolution optical imagery, described as useful for visually identifying vessels; nearby labels include “Optical images” and “High-resolution.” The lower-left section depicts nighttime optical imagery (VIIRS), which detects lights used to attract catch or conduct night operations; nearby labels include “Detect lights” and “Global daily coverage.” The upper-right section depicts AIS (Automatic Identification Systems), described as a collision-avoidance system that constantly transmits a vessel’s location at sea and can identify and track fishing vessels; nearby labels include “Track movements” and “Identify vessels.” The lower-right section depicts radar imagery (SAR), described as identifying large metal vessels and penetrating clouds; nearby labels include “Penetrate clouds” and “Identify metal vessels.” The orange circular framework and inward-pointing arrow motifs visually connect these data sources and capabilities to the central vessel. The accompanying note states that public-intent data include satellite data and private-intent data include data from trawlers’ collision-avoidance systems.
regions.limitations: The infographic is schematic and gives no numerical measurements or plotted data. The page’s title, source, and note are adjacent to the diagram; source credits Global Fishing Watch and dates the infographic July 8, 2020.
